+: Dr. Bonar may just be the most knowledgeable instructor in all of Bilkent.

+: The texts he assigned were often complex and long, but all of them were well worth the read, meaningful, and horizon-expanding.

+: I wouldn't have read these texts otherwise but coupled with the background and readings of the texts he provides, they help you gain new perspectives on many things. 

+: He, unlike any of my friends' instructors, has an appointment system set up for the tasks. This helped me immensely as the rest of my curriculum consisted of uncertain times, often subject to change. It may be hard to keep track of, but only if you are irresponsible.

+: His corrections and input is always straight to the point, leaving no question as to what needs improving and in what way.

: Although always fair when considering it limited to his section, his grading is on the stingy side. You might find yourself working significantly harder, and reading much longer texts, and generally putting in more effort when compared to your friends, and still getting a lower grade point average.

+: Even so, you find yourself learning significantly more and having more meaningful lectures compared to your friends. All things considered, I would strongly advise taking this course from him if you aren't in desperate need of higher grades or dislike reading.

Maybe the IEEE format of writing and researching about a complete case are beneficial for engineers in their future life. The workload of the course is not much which gives a chance of forgetting the course in the semester for students. The most problematic part is attendence. There is 80% attendence obligation.

It makes sense to have a course that focuses on communication skills. But this is a really bad implementation of the idea. The course is a one big vague project that includes, research, writing and presentations. At any point there are too many goals and requirements to consider. It is a burden and reduces the chances of learning anything. A better redesign for the course would allow students to focus on specific skills. This course tries to achieve too much. It aims to be a total transformational experience for engineering students. As a result it fails.

This course took a considerable chunk of my time during the semester, yet I can easily say I have learned a lot by preparing the presentations and the reports. Identifying a problem, working on it, proposing solutions, analyzing it accordingly with criteria and reaching a conclusion really gave me a feeling of completing a project. Being able to give presentations is critical for engineering department, considering many individuals here have weak communication skills.
A negative aspect can be the numerous parts you should pay attention to during the stages.
